preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(x, int) and 1 <= x <= 10**9 for x in a) and all(isinstance(x, int) and 1 <= x <= 10**9 for x in b) and len(a) == n and len(b) == m and 1 <= n <= 2*10**5 and 1 <= m <= 2*10**5 and all(b[i] < b[i+1] for i in range(m-1))
preconditions.description: Input consists of two integers n and m (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 2·10^5), followed by n integers a₁, ..., aₙ (1 ≤ aᵢ ≤ 10⁹) and m strictly ascending integers b₁, ..., bₘ (1 ≤ bᵢ ≤ 10⁹).

postconditions.expression: stdout == str(count_ways(a, b) % 998244353) and count_ways(a, b) == sum(1 for partition in valid_partitions(a, b) if len(partition) == m)
postconditions.description: The output is the number of valid ways to partition array a into m consecutive subarrays such that the minimum of the i-th subarray equals bᵢ, modulo 998244353. A valid partition is one where each subarray's minimum matches the corresponding bᵢ, and all elements are assigned to exactly one subarray.

postconditions.expression: all(len(subarray) >= 1 for subarray in partition) and all(min(subarray) == b[i] for i, subarray in enumerate(partition)) and sum(len(subarray) for subarray in partition) == n
postconditions.description: For each valid partition, every subarray must be non-empty, its minimum must equal the corresponding bᵢ, and the total length of all subarrays must equal n.
